evidence.field: 子; Shang oracle glyph candidate, direct image link, and reuse rights
evidence.text: The Commons description identifies the file as a modern SVG depiction of 子 in Shang oracle script style, lists Sinica Database, Chinese Etymology, and CUHK as source collections, and states CC0/public-domain dedication. The exact direct image URL is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/41/%E5%AD%90-oracle.svg; the web tool resolved it from the page’s Original file link but could not render the SVG because of its image content type.
evidence.title: File:子-oracle.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: 子; Western Zhou bronze glyph candidate, direct image link, and reuse rights
evidence.text: The Commons description identifies the file as a modern SVG depiction of 子 in Western Zhou bronze script style and states that the representation is public domain. The exact direct image URL is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1b/%E5%AD%90-bronze.svg; the web tool resolved it from the page’s Original file link, but fetching it returned a cache-miss error.
evidence.title: File:子-bronze.svg — Wikimedia Commons

search_audit.outcome: Search executed and description page inspected. The original-file link exposed the exact direct image URL. Image fetch was attempted; the web tool could not render SVG content.
Search executed and description page inspected. The original-file link exposed the exact direct image URL. Image fetch was attempted and failed with a cache-miss error.

gaps: Neither candidate depicts the compound 孩 itself; both illustrate only its 子 semantic component. The dossier states that no dated early form of the compound was located, so these component images must not be presented as forms in a chronological history of 孩.

Both selected files are modern redrawings, not photographs of ancient artifacts. The actual pixels were not visually inspected by the researcher; the oracle image fetch failed at rendering and the bronze image fetch returned a cache miss.

items.period: Shang period script style (as identified by the Commons description)
items.caption: Modern redraw of 子 in Shang oracle script style, illustrating the semantic component associated with child or infant; this is not an early form of the full character 孩.
items.alt: A modern vector redraw of an oracle-script 子 glyph.
items.selection_reason: Supports the dossier’s account of 子 as the semantic component and is explicitly sourced and openly licensed on its Commons description page.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public-domain dedication per the Commons file description.

items.period: Western Zhou period script style (as identified by the Commons description)
items.caption: Modern redraw of 子 in Western Zhou bronze script style, a second example of the semantic component; it does not document the compound 孩’s historical graphic sequence.
items.alt: A modern vector redraw of a bronze-script 子 glyph.
items.selection_reason: Provides a distinct script-style example of the semantic component with documented public-domain status; its provenance page was inspected, although the image fetch itself was unsuccessful.
items.rights: Public domain per the Commons file description.

limitations.text: Both candidates illustrate 子 rather than 孩. They can support discussion of the semantic component only and cannot establish early attestations or graphic development of the whole character.
The web tool did not render or visually inspect the selected SVG pixels; the oracle fetch reported unsupported SVG content type and the bronze fetch returned a cache-miss error.
